name: US-100 ultrasonic distance sensor (UART mode)
description: Ultrasonic distance sensor (about 2–450 cm, ±(3 mm + 1 %)) with a built-in temperature sensor for speed-of-sound compensation. With the mode jumper on the back fitted it talks 9600-baud UART: send 0x55 to get the distance in mm (2 bytes, high first), 0x50 to get the temperature (1 byte, °C + 45). Runs on 2.4–5.5 V, so it works directly with 3.3 V boards. Sold as: Adafruit US-100 Ultrasonic Distance Sensor - 3V or 5V Logic (#4019), 5-pin header VCC, Trig/TX, Echo/RX, GND, GND, jumper fitted for UART mode.
eli5: Chirps a sound too high to hear and times the echo to tell your board how far away things are, then sends the answer as numbers over a serial wire.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 2.4–5.5 V (3.3 V or 5 V); logic levels follow VCC

pins.name: Trig/TX
pins.description: UART mode: the module's serial INPUT. Connect to the board's UART TX (TX to TX, as printed). Trigger input with the jumper removed

pins.name: Echo/RX
pins.description: UART mode: the module's serial OUTPUT. Connect to the board's UART RX (RX to RX, as printed). Echo output with the jumper removed

pins.name: GND2
pins.description: Second ground pin, joined to GND on the module

buildNotes: Fit the mode jumper on the back for UART mode; without it the module behaves like an HC-SR04 (trigger/echo pulses) and will not answer serial commands.
The pin labels are the reverse of usual UART practice: wire the board's TX to Trig/TX and the board's RX to Echo/RX.
9600 baud, 8-N-1. Send 0x55 and read 2 bytes: distance mm = high × 256 + low. Send 0x50 and read 1 byte: temperature °C = byte − 45.
Allow up to about 100–300 ms for the distance reply (longer for far objects); readings outside about 20–4500 mm are not reliable.
Powered from 3.3 V it outputs 3.3 V logic, so it is safe on ESP32 and Pico pins.

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
import time
from us100 import US100

# US-100 quirk: board TX -> Trig/TX, board RX -> Echo/RX
u = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=9600, tx=Pin({TRIG_TX}), rx=Pin({ECHO_RX}))
sensor = US100(u)
while True:
    d = sensor.distance_mm()
    t = sensor.temperature()
    if d is not None and t is not None:
        print('D=%dmm T=%dC' % (d, t))
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Reports the distance and temperature set on the sliders
